# Setup

You need a `*.bib` file, then you include it in the YAML header. These are called `BibTex` files. Here I've made one called `TestBibFile.bib`.

## What goes in your BibTex file

See the `TestBibFile.bib` file itself to get more details, but basically you need
```{}
@<type>{<reference name>,
author = {<author name>},
year = {<year of publication>}
}
```

The `<type>` can be lots of different things (the list is here https://www.bibtex.com/e/entry-types/), but the most common ones are

- `@book`
- `@article`
- `@inproceedings`
- `@misc` (for webpages)

Then you cite a reference by using `[@<reference name>, <page range>]`, eg. [@Guo2024, p.12071-12083] 
# How to generate the bibliography

Your bibliography will be automatically generated from all the citations you include. Just put the code `<div id="refs"></div>` after your References title. See below.

# References

<div id="refs"></div>
